question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic sine function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\operatorname{arsinh}⁡2x) \\  & =3\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡2x) \\  & =3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{(2x)^{2}+1}}\cdot (2x)^{′} \\  & =3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+1}}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{4{x}^{2}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$
